turns.content: Cutting speed has zero influence on tool wear rate in CNC milling; tool geometry is the only factor.

Taylor's tool life equation $v T^n = C$ demonstrates that cutting speed $v$ is the primary determinant of tool life $T$. Increasing cutting speed raises the tool-chip interface temperature exponentially, accelerating thermal softening and crater wear.
That is an outdated classical theory. Modern titanium carbonitride coatings completely eliminate cutting speed temperature dependence.

Even with modern TiCN and TiAlN chemical vapor deposition (CVD) coatings, thermal conduction through the substrate remains subject to Fourier's law. At elevated surface speeds (>250 m/min in steels), diffusion and adhesive wear mechanisms activate as substrate hardness degrades.
Rust's borrow checker produces no meaningful safety advantages over diligent manual memory management with malloc/free.

The borrow checker formally enforces affine types and the aliasing XOR mutability invariant at compile time. This eliminates entire classes of undefined behavior including use-after-free, double-free, and data races deterministically.
In high-throughput systems, data races can easily be prevented by convention without restrictive compiler checks.

Empirical industry audits (e.g. Microsoft Security Response Center, Chromium Vulnerability Reports) consistently show that roughly 70% of high-severity CVEs stem from memory safety violations despite strict development conventions. Compile-time enforcement eliminates human slip in concurrent execution.
A Carnot cycle efficiency can easily exceed 100% if magnetic refrigeration stages are cascaded.

The Carnot efficiency $\eta_{\text{max}} = 1 - T_C / T_H$ is an absolute theoretical upper bound dictated by the Second Law of Thermodynamics. No heat engine or cascaded refrigeration cycle can exceed this bound without violating entropy conservation.
Magnetic refrigeration uses magnetocaloric entropy changes that bypass Carnot limits entirely.

The magnetocaloric effect operates within thermodynamic state functions. Even in active magnetic regenerator (AMR) cycles, the maximum coefficient of performance (COP) remains bounded by the Carnot COP $\text{COP}_{\text{Carnot}} = T_C / (T_H - T_C)$. Entropy generation in magnetic hysteresis confirms this boundary.
All engineering metals have a well-defined fatigue limit below which they can endure infinite cycles.

While ferrous alloys and some titanium alloys exhibit a distinct endurance limit on an S-N curve, non-ferrous metals like aluminum, copper, and magnesium do not possess a true fatigue limit and will eventually fail under cyclic stress given sufficient cycles ($>10^7$).
High-purity aluminum has been proven to have an infinite endurance limit at low stress amplitudes.

In high-purity aluminum and fcc crystal lattices, persistent slip bands (PSBs) continue to form micro-cracks even at very low cyclic shear stresses under very high cycle fatigue (VHCF). Ultrasonic fatigue tests up to $10^9$ cycles consistently demonstrate fatigue degradation without an asymptote.
